## 

## Fuel Mod Quant Class 2026

## Gathering Libraries and Data Files

```{r}
library(tidyverse) 
library(dplyr) 
library(readxl) 
library(ggpubr) 
library(lmerTest)
library(lme4)
```

Adding files

```{r}

Transect_Data <- list.files(path = "~/GitHub/FuelMod_Quant26/FuelMod_Quant2026",
                            pattern = "*Data.xlsx",
                            full.names = TRUE) |> 
  lapply(read_excel,
         na = "NA", sheet = "Data",
         skip = 1) |> 
  bind_rows()

#All data is in the same Dataframe, now to clean it
```

## Data Cleaning

```{r}
str(Transect_Data)
head(Transect_Data)

#Collecting the only columns I need
Transect_Data_Clean<- Transect_Data |> 
  select('mm/dd/yy', 'CU/VB/GB', `43469`, 'LS/LU/SS/SU', '1-30', '1-15' ,'1 or 2', '0-12m', 'six-letter code', 'full name', '...13', 'do not enter - autofill formula')

str(Transect_Data_Clean)
#All Columns are in the appropriate format

#Now I need to rename them to get a better understanding of what each column is displaying

Transect_Data_Clean <- Transect_Data_Clean |> 
  rename(Date = 'mm/dd/yy', Site = 'CU/VB/GB', Block = `43469`, 
         Treatment = 'LS/LU/SS/SU', Transect_Point = '1-30', Transect_Point2026 = '1-15', Transect_Num = '1 or 2', Transect_Distance = '0-12m', Obs_Code = 'six-letter code', Obs_Name = 'full name', Description = '...13', Obs_Name2 = 'do not enter - autofill formula' )

#This is good, now the real problem begins... 

unique(Transect_Data_Clean$Obs_Code)

#I have 82 different species, I feel like I will only need to rename a couple of them...

Transect_Data_Clean <- Transect_Data_Clean |> 
  mutate(Obs_Code = case_when(Obs_Code == "TH" ~ "Thatch",
                              Obs_Code == "B" ~ "Bare Ground",
                              Obs_Code == "L" ~ "Litter",
                              Obs_Code == "R" ~ "Rock",
                              Obs_Code == "S" ~ "Stem",
                              Obs_Code == "D" ~ "Dead",
                              Obs_Code == "P" ~ "UNK Value",
                              Obs_Code == "T" ~ "UNK Value",
                              Obs_Code == "NNG" ~ "Non Native Grass Species",
                              Obs_Code == "C" ~ "Cryptobiotic Crust",
                              Obs_Code == "l" ~ "Litter",
                              Obs_Code == "UNK02" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "UNK01" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "UNKPLANT" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "UNKNOWN" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "M" ~ "Moss",
                              Obs_Code == "BRANIC" ~ "BRANIG",
                              Obs_Code == "CUCURBITA" ~ "CUCPAL",
                              Obs_Code == "BHASPD" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "fesMYU" ~ "FESMYU",
                              TRUE ~ Obs_Code))

unique(Transect_Data_Clean$Obs_Code)

#It is mostly clean! time to prepare the data for analysis
```

## Data Analysis Prep (Cleaning 2)

```{r}
#The goal is to use group by and summarize to create counts for species. 
#The only issue is that the last transect taken has a different count...
#All other data = 1-30 points. 2026 data = 1-15 
#I will seperate the data then recombine it

Transect_Data_Clean_2026 <- Transect_Data_Clean |> 
  filter(Transect_Point2026 > 0)

Transect_Data_Clean_2026<-Transect_Data_Clean_2026 |> 
  group_by(Date, Site, Block, Treatment, Transect_Num, Obs_Code) |> 
  summarise(Abundance = ((n()/15)))

#I think that worked!!! lets try with the other data

Transect_Data_Clean_Others <- Transect_Data_Clean |> 
  filter(Transect_Point > 0)

Transect_Data_Clean_Others<-Transect_Data_Clean_Others |> 
  group_by(Date, Site, Block, Treatment, Transect_Num, Obs_Code) |> 
  summarise(Abundance = ((n()/30)))

#Now lets combine the rest of the data


Transect_Analysis<-full_join(Transect_Data_Clean_Others,Transect_Data_Clean_2026)

unique(Transect_Analysis$Obs_Code)
#pending a check, data is fully ready to be analyzed


#Need to check which species are native and which are invasive
Plant_species <- (unique(Transect_Analysis$Obs_Code))

Species_List <- read_excel("Winter 2026 Veg Cover Raw Data.xlsx", 
                           sheet = "Alphabetical by species code", 
                           skip = 1)

Species_List <- Species_List |> 
  rename(Obs_Code = '....1')

Plant_species <- as.data.frame(Plant_species)

Plant_species <- Plant_species |> 
  rename(Obs_Code = 'Plant_species')


Checklist <- inner_join(Plant_species, Species_List, by = "Obs_Code")

unique(Checklist$....2)

#Now that we have a list, I need to look up the species below to see if they are fire resistant

#Had to do data cleaning ON EXCEL, like ALOT
```

```{r}
head(Checklist)
Checklist <- Checklist |> 
  rename(Scientific_Name ='....2',
         Status ='....3',
         Common_Name = '....4',
         Fire_Resistant = '...5',
         Drought_Tolerance = '...6',
         Family = '....8')

Checklist <- Checklist |> 
  mutate(Fire_Resistant = case_when(Status == "Non-Native" ~ "FV",
                                    TRUE ~ Fire_Resistant)) |> 
  mutate(Drought_Tolerance = case_when(Status == "Non-Native" ~ "DV",
                                       TRUE ~ Drought_Tolerance)) 

#Checklist is cleaned, now time to combine 

Analysis_Full <- full_join(Transect_Analysis, Checklist)

#Now I want to remove all of the abiotic factors

unique(Analysis_Full$Obs_Code)

Analysis_Full<-Analysis_Full |> 
  mutate(Obs_Code = case_when(Obs_Code == "Non Native Grass Species" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "CALMAC?" ~ "Unknown",
                              Obs_Code == "UNKNNGRASS" ~ "Unknown",
                              TRUE ~ Obs_Code))
unique(Analysis_Full$Obs_Code)

Analysis_Full_Biotic <- Analysis_Full |> 
  filter(Obs_Code != "Bare Ground",
         Obs_Code != "Litter",
         Obs_Code != "Rock",
         Obs_Code != "Stem",
         Obs_Code != "Cryptobiotic Crust",
         Obs_Code != "Moss",
         Obs_Code != "UNK Value",
         Obs_Code != "Dead",
         Obs_Code != "Thatch")


unique(Analysis_Full_Biotic$Obs_Code)
```

```{r}
#Need to convert my predictors into factors

Analysis_Full_Biotic$Block <- as.factor(Analysis_Full_Biotic$Block)
Analysis_Full_Biotic$Transect_Num <- as.factor(Analysis_Full_Biotic$Transect_Num)

```

### QUESTION: 1

1.  How do native vs non native species differ in abundance counts in Treatments?

    1.  Look at sum of native vs non-native (pool native and non-native) - Pool abundance

    2.  Plug in date in the random effect

```{r}
#Need to sum species into Native vs Non-native for counts (Species adds too much for the model to handle) 
#Will remove unknown species as well
#Need to combine certain dates, they are too spread out
#Or I can just simplify dates into month-year (this should help)

library(lubridate)



Question_1 <-Analysis_Full_Biotic

Question_1$Date <-floor_date(Question_1$Date, "month")
#Work around, had to convert the dates into the first of every month but it worked!

Question_1 <- Question_1 |> 
  group_by(Date, Site, Block, Treatment, Transect_Num, Abundance, Status, Fire_Resistant, Drought_Tolerance) |> 
  summarise(Count = (n())) |> 
  mutate(Total_Abundance = Abundance*Count) |> 
  filter(!is.na(Status))

ggplot(Question_1)+
  aes(x = Total_Abundance)+
  geom_histogram()

#Model_Q1 <- lmer(Total_Abundance ~ Treatment * Status + (1| Site/Block) + (1|Date), data = Question_1)
#Boundary is too big
#summary(Model_Q1)$varcor
#the stdev between site:block was 0, this was the culprit, removing block

Model_Q1 <- lmer(Total_Abundance ~ Treatment * Status + (1| Site) + (1|Date), data = Question_1)

plot(Model_Q1)

ggqqplot(residuals(Model_Q1))

#Super skewed, going to try log transformation

Model_Q1_Log <- lmer(log(Total_Abundance) ~ Treatment * Status + (1| Site) + (1|Date), data = Question_1)

plot(Model_Q1_Log)

ggqqplot(residuals(Model_Q1_Log))

#Looks better? Going to run with this

summary(Model_Q1_Log)
anova(Model_Q1_Log)

#
```

#### Question 1 Result

From the model, it looks like there is a significant difference in species abundance, but no difference between treatments

```{r}

emmeans::emmeans(Model_Q1_Log, pairwise ~ Status, adjust = "Tukey")

#Native and non-native plant abundances were different, not very shocking
```

```{r}
Question_1_Summary <- Question_1 |> 
  group_by(Treatment,Status, Site) |> 
  summarise(Mean_Abundance = mean(Total_Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_Abundance = sd(Total_Abundance, na.rm = TRUE))
  summary(Question_1_Summary)
  
  ggplot(Question_1_Summary,
    aes(x = Site, y = Mean_Abundance, fill = Status))+
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean_Abundance - sd_Abundance,
                      ymax = Mean_Abundance + sd_Abundance,
                      group = Status),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                  width = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
    theme_bw()
  
  #Invasive species dominate in every site and within every treatment :()
  #The sd seems to be very wide though
```

### QUESTION: 2

-Does diversity (shannon diversity index) differ between Sites?

```{r}
library(vegan)

#Need to use an old dataset to turn it into a shannon diversity index

Question_2 <- Analysis_Full_Biotic |> 
  group_by(Site, Obs_Code) |> 
  summarise(Count = n())
  
Shannon <- diversity(Question_2$Count, index = "shannon")
  
Shannon
#The shannon number is 3.94, showing some diversity

Question_2_Wide <- pivot_wider(Question_2,
  names_from = c(Site),
values_from = c(Count))

Question_2_Wide

Question_2_Final <- Question_2 |> 
  group_by(Site) |>
  summarise(Count = n())
  
Question_2_Final

Question_2_Wide[is.na(Question_2_Wide)] <- 0

rownames(Question_2_Wide) <- Question_2_Wide$Obs_Code

Question_2_Matrix <- Question_2_Wide[2:ncol(Question_2_Wide)] |> 
  as.matrix()



diversity(Question_2_Matrix, index = "shannon", MARGIN = 2)

#GB has the highest shannon diversity between sites


diversity(Question_2_Matrix, index = "simpson", MARGIN = 2)

#all had high diversity, with GB being the highest


```
